finding.title: Add Locale('he') RTL variant to tutor_pin_reset_screen_l1_test.dart and tutor_pin_setup_screen_l1_test.dart
finding.why: Neither file contains a single Locale('he') pump, so RTL/overflow regressions in the PIN-reset and PIN-setup screens (part of the same security-sensitive tutor-PIN flow) are invisible to this suite. The sibling test in the same directory, tutor_pin_entry_gate_l1_test.dart, DOES carry a Hebrew group ('he locale: renders PIN entry screen without overflow or crash') proving the flow is expected to be RTL-tested — these two screens are the odd ones out. coding-standards.md's own TQ-3 rationale states this app ships RTL/overflow fixes 'every audit wave', so an LTR-only gap here is a live, stated-cost risk, not a hypothetical one.
finding.recommendation: Add a `he` locale smoke test to each file mirroring tutor_pin_entry_gate_l1_test.dart's Hebrew group (pump with Locale('he'), assert no exception and the Scaffold/key text renders).
acceptance_criteria: tutor_pin_reset_screen_l1_test.dart and tutor_pin_setup_screen_l1_test.dart each gain a testWidgets case pumping Locale('he') that asserts the screen renders without throwing.

finding.title: Delete the dead permanently-skipped test in w3_41_tutor_security_rules_test.dart

evidence.quote:
skip:
            'Structural check superseded by allow create: if isOwner(uid) '

finding.why: The test 'completions write is still owner-only despite tutor read access' (lines 331-345) is permanently skipped with a comment saying it is superseded by the very next test ('...guard is not weakened by C2 change', line 347+), which already covers the same invariant. It carries no Linear id, so it sits inert in CI output forever; a reader scanning for security-boundary coverage sees a 'skipped' result next to a security-sounding name and cannot tell at a glance whether that indicates a real unverified gap or accepted redundancy.
finding.recommendation: Delete the skipped test block; the following test already asserts the same isOwner(uid)-only invariant.
acceptance_criteria: grep for 'skip:' in w3_41_tutor_security_rules_test.dart returns nothing.

finding.title: Replace ws3_3e_dual_role_fix_test.dart's naive method-body string slice with depth-matched brace extraction
finding.why: The helper extracts a Dart method's body by finding the FIRST line that is exactly two spaces + '}' after the method start, instead of counting brace depth. It happens to work today only because _isTutorSession is a one-line method; the same fragile logic is duplicated a second time in the same file (AC2, ~line 72-75) instead of being factored out. The codebase already has the correct depth-counting version right next door — _extractRuleBlock in w3_41_tutor_security_rules_test.dart:438-459 — that this file doesn't reuse. If _isTutorSession ever grows a nested block whose closing brace lands at the same 2-space indent, the slice truncates early and the isNot(contains(...)) assertion would pass regardless of what the unseen remainder of the method does.
finding.recommendation: Extract _extractRuleBlock-style depth-counting into a shared test helper and use it for method-body extraction here instead of the raw indexOf heuristic; de-duplicate the two inline copies in this file.
acceptance_criteria: ws3_3e_dual_role_fix_test.dart's method-body extraction uses depth-matched brace counting (or a shared helper), with a regression case where the target method contains a nested block closing at the same indent.
